correctness.rationale: For \(A=\lambda P\), each exact Nyström approximation is \(\lambda\) times an orthogonal projector, hence its spectral function is \(c\) times that projector. Conditionally on all but one Gaussian columns, the held-out residual energy is chi-square with \(d=r-k+1\) degrees of freedom. Conditionally on all but two columns, the two held-out energies reduce to independent standard Gaussian radii and the squared-direction cosine in dimension \(q=d+1\); its beta moments give \(\operatorname{Cov}(X_i,X_j)=2d/(d+3)\). Exact unbiasedness, variance, sample-indicator mean and rank-plus-one exactness follow algebraically. Standalone code checks moment identities with exact rationals, projector geometry on rational instances, and direct seeded Gaussian simulations. None of the infinite-parameter claims relies on finite testing. The proof covers one probe, for which the posterior indicator is undefined, and any ambient dimension at least the rank.

value.rationale: The finite-rank flat-spectrum model is the natural rank-saturation and equal-eigenvalue benchmark for an exchangeable Nyström trace estimator. It exposes a nontrivial high-rank behavior: at exactly the rank in unnormalized Gaussian probes, the full approximation is exact while the trace estimator retains squared risk approaching \(c^2/2\), and the standard leave-one-out squared-error indicator shrinks to zero in expectation. The exact factor supplies a mean-unbiased risk diagnostic for this benchmark, while the rank-plus-one boundary separates exact full-matrix recovery from estimator saturation. The model is motivated and not an arbitrary coordinate slice. The known normalized-probe workaround and absence of generic claims are disclosed.
